- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < 0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive but price history shows mean reversion (last 5 prices trending down), model overconfidently forecasts upward; apply downward bias of 1–3% per negative sentiment signal.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or weak (avg sentiment < 0.05) and price history shows consolidation; add 1–2% to forecast to account for hidden volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion; use 7-day rolling average as a correction anchor for final 10–15 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 2+ consecutive negative sentiment), model tends to ignore sentiment and forecast linearly — force a 5–10% downward adjustment.
